title: Zariski log stalks and extension of units to geometric stalks
statement:
Let $X$ be a locally Noetherian scheme [pqf-def-locnoeth], let $N_Z\to(\mathcal O_X,\cdot)$ be a log structure on its Zariski site, and let $N$ be its associated log structure on the small etale site [def-trf-fs-log-blowup]. Here log structure and associated log structure have the same unit-isomorphism and sheafified pushout meaning as in [def-trf-fs-log-blowup], using open subsets and open covers for the Zariski site. Assume $N$ is fine saturated. Let $x\in X$ and let $\bar x$ be a geometric point over $x$ [def-weil-geometric-point]. Put $A=\mathcal O_{X,x}$, $B=\mathcal O_{X,\bar x}$, $L=(N_Z)_x$, and $\overline L=L/A^\times$, where geometric stalks are as in [def-weil-pbc-geometric-stalks] and quotient by units is as in [def-trf-fine-fan-blowup]. Regard $N$ as the etale log structure $L_{\mathrm{Et}}$ of [lem-trf-zariski-prelog-logification-comparison] for $\mathcal P=N_Z$ and $\beta$ its structure map; since $N_Z$ is a log structure, the set $E_x$ there is the image of $A^\times$ in $L$. Its stalk formulas give the canonical isomorphisms
$$L\oplus_{A^\times}B^\times\xrightarrow{\sim}N_{\bar x},\qquad \overline L\xrightarrow{\sim}N_{\bar x}/B^\times,$$
where the pushout is the quotient of $L\times B^\times$ by $(l+a,b)\sim(l,\iota(a)b)$ for $a\in A^\times$ and the first map sends $[l,b]$ to the image of $l$ times the canonical unit $b$; here $\iota:A^\times\to B^\times$ is induced by the local map $A\to B$. These identifications respect the structural maps, germs of Zariski sections, and the maps from units. Then $L$ and $N_{\bar x}$ are integral monoids, their units are respectively $A^\times$ and $B^\times$, and the canonical map $L\to N_{\bar x}$ is injective. If $q:Q\to N$ is a chart by a fine saturated monoid on a pointed etale neighborhood of $\bar x$, and $E=\{q_0\in Q:\alpha(q(q_0))_{\bar x}\in B^\times\}$, they identify
$$\overline L\simeq (Q-E)/E^{\mathrm{gp}}$$
compatibly with the chart germ. Here $E$ is a face, $Q-E$ denotes localization inside $Q^{\mathrm{gp}}$, and $E^{\mathrm{gp}}$ is the subgroup generated by $E$.

source.place: Expose VI 1.1, printed p.69; Expose VIII section 3 opening convention, printed p.97, and 3.3.2--3.3.4(ii), printed pp.106--107: associated Zariski log structures and charts. Agent extraction of the change-of-units stalk formula, not a separately numbered assertion.

proof.text: Write $G=A^\times$, $H=B^\times$, and $M=N_{\bar x}$. The log axiom identifies $G$ with the elements of $L$ whose structural image is invertible: an inverse germ of a function is represented on a sufficiently small open neighbourhood, and the sheaf unit-isomorphism then gives its unique logarithmic germ. A monoid unit has invertible structural image, so $L^\times=G$. The same argument on pointed etale neighbourhoods gives $M^\times=H$. Apply [lem-trf-zariski-prelog-logification-comparison] with $\mathcal P=N_Z$. Its $E_x$ is exactly $G$, and its Zariski logification is $N_Z$: the inverse of $l\mapsto[l,1]$ is $[l,a]\mapsto l+a$. Its etale comparison and stalk clauses therefore give $M=L\oplus_G H$ with $[l,b]\mapsto j(l)b$, where $j:L\to M$ is the germ map. The structural map is $[l,b]\mapsto\iota(\alpha_L(l))b$, by the defining prelog pushout. These formulas also identify the two canonical unit maps.

source.place: VI 1.1, p.69; VIII section 3 opening, p.97, and 3.3.2, p.106; change-of-site and stalk clauses of the cited node.

proof.text: The relations in $L\oplus_G H$ are the orbits of the group $G$ acting on $L\times H$ by $a\cdot(l,b)=(l+a,\iota(a)^{-1}b)$, writing the monoid law of $L$ additively and that of units multiplicatively. Indeed each generator of the pushout congruence is an orbit relation, and the orbit relation is a monoid congruence because the action is by translation by unit pairs. In particular equality of two classes is witnessed by one $a\in G$, without any cancellation hypothesis on $L$. The maps $L/G\to M/H$, $[l]\mapsto[[l,1]]$, and $M/H\to L/G$, $[[l,b]]\mapsto[l]$, are well defined: a pushout relation changes $l$ by a unit, and multiplication by $H$ changes only $b$. Their composites are identities, since $[[l,b]]=[[l,1]]$ modulo $H$. This proves the claimed characteristic isomorphism with its canonical germ formula.

source.place: VI 1.1, p.69; agent-written orbit and quotient calculation for the change-of-units pushout.

proof.text: Now take any chart $q:Q\to N$ as in the statement. Apply [lem-trf-chart-face-localization-logification] with its ring denoted here by $B$ and its log stalk by $M$. It states that $E$ is a face and, with $R=Q-E$ and $U=E^{\rm gp}$, gives $R\oplus_U H\simeq M$ and $R/U\simeq M/H$, sending the class of a chart germ to that same class in $M/H$. Consequently, composing the second isomorphism with the inverse of step 2 yields $\overline L\simeq (Q-E)/E^{\rm gp}$ with the required chart compatibility. Moreover [lem-trf-fs-face-sharpening] states that $R$ is fs with $R^\times=U$. In particular $R$ embeds into $Q^{\rm gp}$ and is cancellative. Such a chart exists at $\bar x$ by the definition of an fs log structure [def-trf-fs-log-blowup]; fix one for the next step.

source.place: VI 1.1, p.69; VIII 3.1.1--3.1.5, pp.98--99, and 3.3.4(ii), p.107; localized-chart and fs face-sharpening statements.

proof.text: Use the presentation $M\simeq R\oplus_U H$ just obtained. Let $\gamma:U\to H$ be the chart structure map on units. As in step 2, equality of $[r,h]$ and $[r',h']$ means $r'=r+u$ and $h'=\gamma(u)^{-1}h$ for some $u\in U$. Suppose $[r,h]+[t,k]=[r',h']+[t,k]$. The orbit description supplies $u$ with $r'+t=r+t+u$ and $h'k=\gamma(u)^{-1}hk$. Cancellation in $R\subset Q^{\rm gp}$ gives $r'=r+u$, and cancellation in the group $H$ gives $h'=\gamma(u)^{-1}h$. Thus $[r,h]=[r',h']$. Hence $M$ is cancellative and integral: for a commutative cancellative monoid, equality of two elements in its group completion means $m+t=m'+t$ for some $t$, and cancellation gives $m=m'$. No injectivity of $\gamma$ was assumed.

source.place: VIII 3.1.1--3.1.5, pp.98--99; agent-written cancellation calculation in the localized chart pushout.

proof.text: To control the units map, apply [lem-sfb-space-strict-local-flatness] to the scheme $X$, regarded as an algebraic space over itself through its representable sheaf $h_X$ [def-trf-scheme-algebraic-space], and to its identity etale chart. Its canonical stalk identification gives $B\simeq A^{\rm sh}$ for the residue-field embedding specified by $\bar x$. The map from $A$ is the canonical one: both maps send a germ of a regular function to its etale germ. The ring $A$ is a local ring of a scheme, and $\bar x$ specifies a separable closure of its residue field in its algebraically closed field. Thus [lem-sc-strict-henselization-faithfully-flat] applies and makes $A\to B$ faithfully flat. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-faithfully-flat-ideal-contraction] with the zero ideal to conclude that $A\to B$ is injective. Restricting this injective map to units proves that $\iota:G\to H$ is injective.

source.place: Tag 04KF (lemma-describe-etale-local-ring), specialized to schemes; Tag 07QM (lemma-dumb-properties-henselization), part (1); Tag 05CK (lemma-faithfully-flat-universally-injective), zero-ideal case.

proof.text: If $j(l)=j(l')$, step 1 gives $[l,1]=[l',1]$ in the unit pushout. Step 2 supplies $a\in G$ with $l'=l+a$ and $1=\iota(a)^{-1}$. Step 5 gives $a=1_G$, whose image is the identity $0_L$, so $l'=l$. Thus $j$ is injective. If $l+t=l'+t$ in $L$, apply $j$, cancel $j(t)$ in the integral monoid $M$ from step 4, and use injectivity to obtain $l=l'$. The group-completion criterion in step 4 then proves that $L$ is integral. All compatibility assertions follow from the formulas already proved: the pushout sends $[l,b]$ to $j(l)b$, the characteristic sends $[l]$ to $[j(l)]$, and the chart comparison sends a chart element to its germ class. Applying the structural maps sends both representatives to $\iota(\alpha_L(l))b$; taking $b=1$ gives the Zariski germ map and taking $l=0$ gives the unit map. This proves every clause.

source.place: VI 1.1, p.69; agent-written injectivity, cancellation and compatibility calculation from steps 1--5.

Step 2: the pushout congruence equals the orbit relation of A^x acting by unit pairs, and the characteristic maps are mutually inverse, with no cancellation used. Step 4: cancellation in R inside Q^gp and in H makes M integral. Step 5: B = A^sh, faithfully flat, hence injective by the zero-ideal case. Step 6: j is injective via step 5, so L is integral; no circularity. Edge cases tested: trivial log structure, standard log point (alpha not injective), nonreduced X.
